checks: Reflection gives depth one half at the cube center in every closed orientation. Any point differing in a coordinate has a shorter coordinate cap, proving unique deepestness. Proper sections have area one and center g.
Except on surface-null intersections with the cutting planes, each pair's two indicators sum to one. Thus the probability-weighted old selector is exactly 1/2, even for signed normal-dependent tests.

The section measure puts w_i/2 at each of ±e_i. Adding half the cube area measure gives (1+w_i)/2 at each sign for A. These are area masses, and no fiber projection or first-moment normalization changes them.

For positive box facet masses b_i, V=(∏b_i)^{1/(d-1)} and ℓ_i=V/b_i have exactly the correct facet products. The dth side of J diverges, and the limiting dth side of A exceeds one by the strict binomial comparison. A translation cannot change either side's projected length.

Exact squared side and volume checks recover the three-dimensional coefficients, including 1369/1300 for A's long side squared and 72/25 for J's. Original 455c254ad09b8374 §§1, 3–4 contains the identical family and finite calibration.

dependencies.hypotheses: The one-body finite law is a probability, all cuts are proper, and the selected old marginal is half the cube's. The general area decomposition gives the section and aggregate measures with no supporting allocations needed.
The explicitly constructed axis boxes are positive and realize the two required area measures. Uniqueness determines the section and aggregate bodies up to translation.
dependencies.reference: Minkowski surface-area uniqueness and Blaschke addition, Gardner, The Brunn–Minkowski inequality, §§6 and 18.2
